chains.title: NME2 binds the alt allele more strongly and distally regulates FAM110B

links.claim: NME2 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele: its own QBiC-SELEX model detects an alt-favoring change (z 28.95, effect +0.573; gate passed), and the alt site is strong (99.1st versus ref 65.7th percentile). NME2 is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (928.15 TPM, rank 1/1626). However, ENCODE did not assay NME2 here and reports no NME2 ChIP peak over the variant in HepG2, so occupancy is unknown; this is SELEX-plus-expression evidence, not ChIP occupancy.

The variant lies in a poorly annotated distal non-coding region: it is intronic/intergenic with no overlapping cCRE, the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away, and there is no HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant in the supplied ENCODE call. This describes the element but does not demonstrate enhancer activity.

The distal element could regulate FAM110B, the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb upstream, and FAM110B is the only nearby gene with an LDL-cholesterol literature hit in the supplied evidence. But GTEx reports no significant eQTL globally or in liver, and the literature hit is not variant-specific, so the element-to-FAM110B link is unsupported.
The relevant cell context is the hepatocyte-like liver cancer line Hep 3B2.1-7, with HepG2 as the ENCODE stand-in; NME2 is highly expressed in this line.

Allele-specific NME2 binding could alter FAM110B expression and thereby LDL cholesterol, but this variant has no GWAS Catalog record, no Open Targets record, and no significant GTEx eQTL globally or in liver. The phenotype link is plausible but not established.

predictions: NME2 ChIP/CUT&RUN or allele-specific footprinting at the variant in Hep 3B2.1-7 shows stronger NME2 occupancy on the alt T allele.

FAM110B expression is allele-specifically altered in hepatocyte-like cells in a NME2-dependent manner.

chains.title: NME2 binds the alt allele more strongly and distally regulates CYP7A1

links.claim: NME2 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele: its own QBiC-SELEX model detects an alt-favoring change (z 28.95, effect +0.573; gate passed), and the alt site is strong. NME2 is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7. However, ENCODE did not assay NME2 here and reports no NME2 ChIP peak over the variant in HepG2, so occupancy is unknown; this is SELEX-plus-expression evidence only.

The variant lies in a poorly annotated distal non-coding region: it is intronic/intergenic with no overlapping cCRE, the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away, and there is no HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant. This describes the element but does not demonstrate regulatory activity.

The distal element could instead regulate CYP7A1, which lies 926.8 kb downstream and is a biological LDL-cholesterol candidate, but there is no chromatin-contact, perturbation, or eQTL evidence linking this variant to CYP7A1. GTEx reports no significant eQTL globally or in liver.
The relevant cell context is the hepatocyte-like liver cancer line Hep 3B2.1-7, with HepG2 as the ENCODE stand-in; NME2 is highly expressed in this line.

Distal NME2-dependent regulation of CYP7A1 in hepatocytes could change bile-acid synthesis and LDL cholesterol, but there is no variant-level GWAS, Open Targets, or eQTL evidence at this variant. The phenotype link is speculative.
